editorial:
Imagine waking up to find out you are now the Pope, but instead of feeling holy, you just feel totally terrified. That is exactly what happens in this quirky story. You get to follow a man who is suddenly the most powerful religious leader in the world, but he is having a massive panic attack. He is convinced he is not the right person for the job and cannot bring himself to step out onto the balcony. To fix this, the church brings in a therapist who does not even believe in God. It is a funny and awkward setup that feels very human, showing that even the highest leaders can feel like imposters who are way over their heads.

The acting is great because it keeps things grounded and realistic rather than making it a cartoon. You will love how the movie balances the stress of the situation with some really dry humor. While it moves a bit slowly at times, the conversations are the best part. If you enjoy stories about people trying to figure out their lives, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night or add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you want the best picture quality possible.
endingExplained: After struggling with his fear and talking with the therapist, the Pope finally decides he cannot do it. He chooses to resign from his position because he knows he is not the right fit for the role. In the end, he steps away from the power and the pressure. It is a happy ending because he finds peace by being honest with himself, proving that doing the right thing is more important than a fancy title.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky stories about identity and faith.
